# Selfware Agent Module — Evidence-Based Review

## 1. `src/agent/last_tool.rs` + `tests/unit/agent/last_tool/last_tool_test.rs`

**Implementation evidence.** The last tool result is stored on the `Agent` struct (not in process-global state) as `Option<LastToolOutput>` (src/agent/last_tool.rs:1–9). Two bounded constants cap retention: `MAX_FULL_OUTPUT_LEN = 16_384` and `MAX_SUMMARY_LEN = 512` (src/agent/last_tool.rs:13, 16). `store_last_tool_output` calls a local `truncate_on_char_boundary` helper that walks backward from the byte limit until `is_char_boundary(b)` is true, then calls `String::truncate(b)` (src/agent/last_tool.rs:42–49). This handles both long ASCII and long multibyte Unicode without panicking. A failed result is retained identically: the `success: bool` field (src/agent/last_tool.rs:29) records the outcome, and `exit_code: Option<i32>` (src/agent/last_tool.rs:31) preserves the shell exit status when applicable. `retrieve_last_tool_output` clones the stored value (src/agent/last_tool.rs:55).

**Test evidence.** `storing_long_output_truncates` (tests/unit/agent/last_tool/last_tool_test.rs:14) asserts exact lengths after truncation of ASCII. `storing_long_multibyte_output_does_not_panic` (tests/unit/agent/last_tool/last_tool_test.rs:42) uses "✿" (3-byte) and "é" (2-byte) to confirm the char-boundary walk produces valid UTF-8 (`std::str::from_utf8(...).is_ok()`). `default_last_tool_output` (line 4) pins the zero-value shape.

**Limitation.** The `default_last_tool_output` test confirms `success` defaults to `false` (the `Default` derive on a bool), meaning a fresh agent with no tool executed yet reports `success: false` rather than a tri-state. This is documented behavior, not a defect.

## 2. `src/agent/task_policy.rs` + `tests/unit/agent/task_policy/task_policy_test.rs`

**Implementation evidence.** `task_is_read_only` (src/agent/task_policy.rs:55) first checks `task_requires_mutation(ctx)`. If mutation is required, it returns true only when BOTH `asks_for_report` (keyword list at lines 63–76) AND `forbids_globally` (via `global_no_edit_prohibition`, line 100) hold. If mutation is NOT required, it returns true when either `asks_for_report` or `forbids_editing` (lines 78–90) match. The `global_no_edit_prohibition` function (src/agent/task_policy.rs:100) checks a fixed list of GLOBAL_MARKERS and uses `prohibition_has_exception` (src/agent/task_policy.rs:130) to detect scoped "other than / except / besides" clauses that keep the task in mutation mode. `policy_envelope` (src/agent/task_policy.rs:240) prefixes guard messages with `[POLICY kind=… retryable=… reason="…"]\n`.

For "review do not code": the word "review" hits `asks_for_report`; "do not edit" hits `forbids_editing`; `task_requires_mutation` returns false (no "implement"/"fix" verb), so the function returns `asks_for_report || forbids_editing` = true.

**Test evidence.** `review_prompt_classifies_read_only` (tests/unit/agent/task_policy/task_policy_test.rs:12) confirms "Review the code in src/agent/ and report findings. Do NOT edit any files." → read-only. `fix_the_bug_classifies_mutation` (line 19) confirms "Fix the bug in parse_port." → not read-only. `prohibition_with_exception_clause_does_not_make_a_task_read_only` (line 30) exercises the c40 case: "Do not change any code other than adding comments" stays mutation. `scoped_prohibition_with_report_word_does_not_flip_an_edit_task` (src/agent/task_policy.rs inline test, line ~310) confirms "fix calculator.py, do not modify test_calculator.py, report the result" stays mutation. `classify_task_policy_stores_decision_at_task_start` (tests/unit/agent/task_policy/task_policy_test.rs:55) verifies the stored decision via `agent.current_task_is_read_only()`.

**Constraints on mutations/completion.** The stored read-only decision gates `current_task_requires_mutation()` (tests/unit/agent/task_policy/task_policy_test.rs:80), which every force-mutation directive and stagnation guard consults. A read-only task with zero mutations is accepted as `NoChange` (non-failure), never `FakeComplete`.
